utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We are informed about the unavailability at this moment of Mr. Piletta-Zanin. The Chamber will consider what course to take and presumably inform you about it this afternoon. Then is there any other issue you'd like to address at this very moment? If not, I'd like to ask the usher to -- yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know if this is the time to address the Chamber, but I have to say that I have just received from the Prosecution a submission of 18 pages, and my colleagues refer in them to documents which make part of Mr. Radinovic's report and documents which represented during his testimony and the documents which the Defence intends to produce. I do not know what will be the Chamber's position with regard to this document, but today I am unable to discuss this brief or any item of these documents, that is, I won't be able to do it until I've gone through this statement, or shall I call it a brief of my learned friends. I do not know what my -- how my colleagues define this document. So I do not think that I could today really tell you what our position is with regard to each individual document. I can do that, of course, but I believe I will need at least two days to go through them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think this is part of the consequence of a lot of documents being produced through this witness. And I do understand that you can't just respond to that on this very moment, and I think it would not be wise to do that because -- but we -- I received -- the Chamber received a copy only a couple of minutes ago. So therefore, even the Chamber would have to prepare more thoroughly. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Usher, could you escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Radovanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Good afternoon as well. May I remind you that you are still bound by your solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The cross-examination will now be continued. Mr. Stamp, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Stamp: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, last night when we broke off I had asked you if you could explain the importance of linking figures from the HSS survey to the 1991 census, and you answered by telling us about matching. I'd like to quickly examine the methodology that you used in respect to linking and your arrival at demographic rates. May I refer you to page 41 of your report, which in -- page 41 in the English version. In the B/C/S version it is in section 4.1, and it is your table 2.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in that table which you presented you purported to show your own comparative survey of casualty rates according to the results of the HSS 1994. And if we could look at the top column of your table here, we see that you have applied the number 2963 for killed, 2573 for natural causes, 11171 for wounded, and you applied that to the overall estimated population of 340.000. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none of what you have just said is correct. None of these figures are mine. These figures were taken over from Mrs. Tabeau's report, and below the table you have the source, table 18 and table 1. I did not attempt any matching at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to listen carefully to what I'm asking. Basically all I'm asking: If these figures that we see in your table 2 are the figures that you used from the Tabeau report. Are they?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The figures for the deaths, those killed and those dying from natural causes, can be found at page 47, table 18 and 19 of the Tabeau report.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there it is made clear that these are figures from HSS 1994 that are linked to the census of 1991.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But they were linked up in a completely wrong way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you have done, in other words, is to apply the smallest possible nominator for deaths, the linked figures to the largest possible denominator, the population of the overall estimated population of 340.000. The question is: Is that a statistically sound approach, or is it just something guaranteed to produce the lowest possible rates? Shouldn't you have compared values that are logically related? For example, the overall death rate to the overall population, or the linked numbers of death of deceased persons to the population that was linked to the 1991 census? Instead of finding the lowest figures for death and applying it to the highest figure for population.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I did that, then I would be also manipulating statistics. But this figure for the killed, naturally died, and wounded, in the opinion of experts represents matched figures. And I'm not going into that. Now we are talking about 1991 census, so Mrs. Tabeau thinks that she's identified them there from 1991 and 1994. When they are matched in such a way, I do not think that this matching procedure is good. Again, it doesn't allow us to establish what is properly identified sample.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... About matching procedures, whether the matching procedures by Tabeau et al. were good, bad, or indifferent, that is not what the question is. The question is: Is it logical, rational, and in proper statistical form to apply figures from two different areas to get the rate? In other words, to use the lowest possible figures for deaths, those that were linked to the 1991 census, to compare it with the highest possible figure for population at risk?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not logical. Only it is the only statistically correct way. What I am saying -- I'm commenting on the size of the population that Mrs. Tabeau estimates, so nothing to do with the figures as such. So we're dealing with one period of time, one thing is statistical estimate yet the other one is a statistical finding. I'm doing it to show what horizontal structure are indicating, because Mrs. Tabeau manipulates vertical structures. So not only that it is logical, it is also statistically the only correct way to do it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. My associate says that under "A" 14:46:28 it says "illogical." But you should ask the witness because the witness said something else. I think she said this was the only logical thing, to avoid any future confusion. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I understood from the translation as well that you said, Madam Radovanovic, that it was the only logical way to do it and the statistically correct way. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to add something to it. One can take estimates into account. Yes, it is possible, but then I don't think that it is the only statistically correct way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just checking on what you said. Could you please look on your screen --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Page 5, line 4, your answer starts as it appears on the screen "it's not logical," but it's our recollection that you said it's the only logical way of doing it. Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, one could have compared the overall numbers for deaths to the overall estimated population. One could have also compared the linked numbers for deaths to the linked numbers of the population at risk. Those --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you consider the general figures for death are the figures that we find in tables 1, 2, and 3, and if we take those estimates into account, one could compare them, but it would serve no purpose because I do not think they are good estimates, nor do we have good figures in tables 1, 2, and 3. Statistically speaking - and I emphasise, I do not think that the matching was correct - there was something that Mrs. Tabeau called identified population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is your answer. Very well. The purpose of establishing a rate, a death rate, for the indictment period involved a comparison with a death rate for the population that resided in Sarajevo prior to 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand what you meant. If you are talking about the comparison that Mrs. Tabeau made between 1991 and 1994 --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll rephrase it. As a matter of statistical form, I suggest to you that if one wants to compare the death rate for the indictment period to the pre-indictment death rate, the appropriate procedure is to apply the linked population from the survey to the linked numbers for deceased during the indictment period.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, I don't understand what you are saying. There are no figures. That is, there are some estimates which are perhaps, known only to Mrs. Tabeau, about the population which between 1992 and 1994 constituted a particular structure. But Mrs. Tabeau otherwise offers us comparisons. In table 16 the mortality rate in Sarajevo in 1990-1991. And in the next table she tells us phenomena within the front lines between the 10th of September and so on and so forth. And in relation, that is my assumption, because that is only statistically correct, assumption, there are no absolute figures there. So here I see only rates. So I presume those rates have to do with the estimated number of the population in 1992-1994. Everything else would completely lack sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you -- I've tried to understand the question that has been put to you. And since you started your answer saying "I don't understand what you are saying," so you're responding to something which was not entirely clear. I do understand the question of Mr. Stamp to be - but he'll certainly correct me if I'm wrong - that if you want to compare a death rate prior to the wartime and during the wartime and if you use for the death rate during the wartime linked numbers of deceased people, that to establish the rate you should also use the linked number of the population involved. And if I do understand him well, he means to say that linking reduces the number of death you take into consideration, and therefore in order to establish a death rate you should apply then the linked number of the population involved as well. That would also, as far as I understand, result in a reduced number compared to the overall total population. Is that a correct understanding of your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that's what Mr. Stamp is asking you: Why do you, for establishing a death rate, do you couple a reduced number of death with a unreduced number of overall population? Could you please answer that question then.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Because there is no -- the linkage of the population for 1992-1994. There is only an estimate, which is 340.000. And these 340.000 were linked with the cases of deaths by violence or by natural causes or wounded and so on and so forth. So that is, we have some -- so many inhabitants who are linked to the census of 1991, and then a particular figure is linked up with them, and it is said from this sample that we have we linked it up with 1991, yet there is nothing for 340.000 inhabitants to be -- to allow you to link those figures, so that is impossible. And you cannot calculate the mortality on the basis of the findings of the census of 1994 with the linked population of 340.000. That does not exist. I don't know if I've made myself clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the question remains that if you say I cannot link the number available to me, there is no possibility of linking, so therefore there'll be no reduction, what sense it makes to compare these figures that are calculated or established on a different basis.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It does, because there is an estimated number of the population. And when you do these things, total number of deaths is divided by the number of the population, average age from the census, and then it is multiplied by 1.000 or 100.000, so -- and that is how these things are done. The censuses are done every ten years, but the mortality rates are done for every year. The census was in 1991, but the death rates are calculated for 1994, 1995, 1996, 1997, and so on and so forth. We do not have the estimated -- we have the estimated number of the population for the period, and it's 340.000, and we have the mortality, and it is -- we know what that figure is. And for that period the rates are calculated by dividing the total mortality with the number of the population, that is, 340.000, then it is divided by 1.000 or by 100, and in this way you get the mortality or the wounding rate or whatever. So the mortality can only be divided. There is no other possibility. And if you do not have an estimated number of the population, then it becomes difficult. But there is an estimated number of the population. So this is, statistically speaking, absolutely correct. Had I used anything else to use the population size of 1991 is completely wrong.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, I'll just suggest to you or indicate to you that the matching rate is indicated in more than one places in the report by Tabeau et al., for example, at page 15 of the establish version, at 81.3 per cent, and it is a simple statistical exercise, a mathematical exercise, to adjust 340.000 to find the amount that was linked. Do you agree with me? Basically, if you know the matching rate, can one just mathematically adjust 340.000 to find the linked population at risk? Can you listen to the question, read it, and then answer it.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will you tell me what page is it in the Serbian version, because --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is at section 3.5, and it is at the third paragraph.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the matching results?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that what it's titled?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. It is indicated there that the matching results were 81.3 per cent. And all the question is: If one is aware of that, isn't it a simple mathematical exercise to adjust the overall total population --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. No, no, no. It's not -- no, it's not. It is a simple mathematical manipulation. This is called the results of the linking of the population, and Mrs. Tabeau says the wounded -- that the wounded, killed, and died that we had were linked with the population census of 1991, and she doesn't say how -- what were the results in relation to the population of 1991. And 81.3 means of a possible 30.000 records, we linked 20.000 wounded and 5.000-something of those others. So 80.1 per cent is what was linked, rather than what they linked it with. So I have to link 30.000, of them 80 per cent I found in 1991 and I say I've linked 81 per cent. Yes, you did link 81 per cent of what you had, but this is with regard to the -- to overall population. But it was linked with 45 -- I don't know how many thousand people, so it could have been only about 5 or 6 per cent. I can't tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Well, before we move on, let me just ask you one question: You have in the second row of your table 2 used 100 as your base figure for setting rates. And in your testimony and at various pages in your report, you repeatedly criticise ET et al. for saying 100.000 when you say 1.000 is the standard in the former Yugoslavia. I'd like you to have a look at this document.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. The table says the share of those who died of natural death and the number of wounded in the population as it was assessed, and then it says in the population of 340.000 the share of a certain category is such and such a figure, et cetera. These are percentages. They aren't rates. Rates are calculated on a base of 1.000 and 100.000. These are percentages, shares. I'm showing that Mrs. Tabeau, with regard to her population estimate, found that there were 0.9 who died. Out of the total number of population in 1992 and 1994, the number who died were 0.9. It was 0.7 for the wounded -- sorry, natural deaths, 0.7 and wounded 0.3. These aren't rates of any kind. These are percentages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Radovanovic, I think Mr. Stamp -- what did Mr. Stamp ask you in his last question? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't repeat it literally, but the question in essence was why did I criticise the rate on the base of 100.000 and the rate that I provided here was calculated on the base of the figure 100. That was the essence of the question. I said that this was not a rate, it's a percentage. I really can't read this, but there is a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the question of Mr. Stamp concerned overall your report, not specifically this table, and your overall criticism that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He quoted table 2 because I wrote something down, and unfortunately I always write something down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Percentages is a figure out of 100, and you use figures out of 100. Here you criticise Tabeau et al. for using figures out of 100.000, because you said that that is not done in respect to statistics in Yugoslavia. Could you have a look at that document which I've just handed to you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For the record, it's P3781.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a publication in the European Journal of Epidemiology by someone, Dr. Jordanka Ananijevic-Pandey of the Institute of Social Medicine, Statistics and Health Research, the Medical Faculty of the University of Belgrade. And there's a translation at the back I'd like to read a passage from the third paragraph. "They evaluate the level of health before the war started, premature mortality from all causes in the former Yugoslavia was analysed by republics and provinces for two periods, 1970 and 1990. The calculation of YPLL - and that is the years lost - rates per 100.000 population 0 to 64 years, crude and age standardised was obtained according to published methodology." You might, madam, be involved in census statistics, but persons involved in the statistics of casualties, victimology, epidemiology, as a standard practice put figures out of 100.000. And in any case, is that something that anyone can easily convert? If a figure is put out of 100.000, could one easily convert it to a figure of 100 or 10.000 or 1.000?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am also involved in statistics. My masters was in mortality and birthrates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I discussed --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Matter of time. The simple question. You could answer yes or no. Is that a simple mathematical thing to convert figures out of 100.000 to figures out of 100 or figures out of 10.000? Is it simple, or is it not?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question hasn't been put correctly whether the numbers on the base of 100.000 can be converted to numbers on the basis of 10.000. Are you asking me whether rates can be calculated on the basis of 100.000 and on the bass of 10.000 and on the base of 1.000 inhabitants? Is that the question you are putting to me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question I asked you is whether or not one could make a mathematical calculation of rates out of 100.000 into rates per 1.000 or per 10.000. Can one do that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can do everything, but the question is whether it makes sense or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what we have here, madam, is a recognised Yugoslav scholar in epidemiology, who was published abroad in important journals of her field abroad, who uses figures out of 100.000 in casualties. And when Tabeau et al., who are experts in their field that you are not an expert in, use the same, you criticise them as dishonest. I suggest to you that that is inappropriate criticism.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the criticism is appropriate and you have shown me an article by a respected expert. I think she is respected. But you haven't provided me with a single figure. It just says that she works out a rate on the base of 100.000 for the population the rate of which is between 0 and 64 years. You can use rates per 100.000, especially in health matters. In epidemiology you have a situation in which you want to represent the mortality of those who choke on food, because such cases are very rare in mortality in general. You have four or five cases a year. The figure used is a figure on the basis of 100.000. This is quite usual. I didn't say that you didn't calculate rates on the basis of 100.000. What I said is that in my opinion, Mrs. Tabeau manipulated the facts because she used figures on the base of 100.000, because statistics in Bosnia and Herzegovina that refer to mortality, official statistics, which were her sources for 1991 and 1990, and she calculated averages on that basis, these figures were on the base of 1.000. I'm not saying she can't do this, but in this report she was manipulative because she used a small number of cases to justify her conclusions. When you have a look at the table that Mrs. Tabeau provides, on the basis of municipalities for 1991, the number of cases is far lower, the number of mortality cases. The number is far lower than the number of the wounded or killed in that period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Answer the question, at least to your satisfaction. Could you move on. At page 24 of your report in the English version - and as from here, I'm going to just ask you to answer my questions as directly as you can. Listen carefully to questions and answer them as you can --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but what is the page in the Serbian version?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's in section 2.1.2, funeral parlour Bakija as a source of mortality data.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The funeral parlour Bakija, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in that section you have a table of sorts that you used to make some comparison with respect to the mortality of Muslims, and you concluded that in the period according to your methods the mortality of Muslims from natural causes was about twice as high as a death by killing. And what basically you did was to find the total number of deaths from killing in the PDS 1994 survey and subtract it from the total of deaths in the Bakija survey. Now, as a statistician, could that approach be justified when the report of Tabeau et al. makes it quite clear that the two surveys do not overlap completely, that they overlap only to the extent of 68 per cent?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you say is not correct. That's not my method. These data was taken from reports made by your experts, and I showed how illogical they were. Please have a look at page 18 in the Serbian version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, let's take it step by step. You took the number from Bakija for buried Muslims for 6.266 and you subtracted the number 2.340, which was the number in PDS 1994 for killed Muslims. So you took one figure from a different independent non-completely overlapping source and subtracted it from the total figure of the second source and you draw conclusions from that as a statistician.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your experts claimed that they used three reliable sources on mortality. The Bakija source is a reliable source according to the experts, and that source -- it says on page 18 of your expert's report that according to the results from the Bakija source they were provided with the figure 6.266 for buried Muslims. I say all right, I agree. And then I take a source that shows the same figures, but it's the second good source, it's the census, the population census of 1994. And that source states that the number of killed Muslims was 2.340.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you stop there.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you stop there, madam. Now, on what basis do you say that you take a source that shows the same figures -- on what basis do you say that the HSS 1994 shows the same figures? Isn't it clear in the report that these are two independent sources, that the HSS 1994 only matched the Bakija to the extent of 68 per cent?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what your experts stated, these are two independent sources that are used, above all when applying that method of catching and catching again, and it's statistics that is a matter of comparing various sources. It's a rule. Such comparisons are rule. The problem here is that such sources are not good. And I'm showing that these various sources which according to your experts are good --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Listen. You've answered the first part of the question that they are two independent sources. The second part of the question is: Isn't it clear to you from the report of Tabeau et al. that the sources overlapped only to the extent of 60 per cent [sic]? Simple.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To whatever extent there was overlapping, they said that the sources were reliable, and it's on the base of these sources that they came to their conclusions in their reports. And on the basis of these figures, they applied new methodologies used in demography and gave assessments whether there is overlapping of 60 per cent or not, well, they should have thought about this. First of all, the source is biased, it's bad. Thirdly, it shows figures for those buried, whatever the location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Answer my question and spare me. The other question is, and it's a simple question that you can answer yes or no: Is the total number in the Bakija database for buried Muslims identical to the total number in HSS 1994 for dead Muslims?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me a question that --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't just answer by saying yes or no for the simple reason that the question doesn't make any sense. These are two independent sources which are used by --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I try to ask you -- there seems to be a lot of confusion. I think the question of Mr. Stamp - but he'll certainly correct me if I'm wrong - is that how could you compare the overall number of people reported to have been deceased with the data contained in a report of the -- at least the data of the Bakija funeral parlour which did not bury all of the people that died? I think that's the question, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It is similar to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Sufficiently similar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the same way that Mrs. Tabeau did this. If you say the source is reliable, I have such information, in the statistics it's a rule, you make comparisons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... To an example to see whether we can agree. Let's just assume that we have a funeral parlour, a small one, which has reliable data as to when people died or what their status was, and they buried 1.000 people, and let's just assume that a general survey of the population would give far higher numbers because it covers the whole of the population and not just a limited number of our small funeral parlour. Would it be of any use and did Ms. Tabeau deduct the numbers from the total survey from the relatively limited numbers of the small funeral parlour? I think that's the issue. You say -- you have told us several times, and I do understand that you say if figures are considered to be reliable you could use them. But reliability of figures does not automatically mean that they cover the whole population. They might be to some extent be comparable and to other extents not comparable. And I think that's the question Mr. Stamp is asking you, how you could deduct from the numbers that appear in a relative -- in a not complete data source, how you could deduct from that the numbers you found in a more extensive data source. That's the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the same way that Mrs. Tabeau did it. She said that she was matching them up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But would you please see where she simply deducts one figure from another.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the deduction isn't what's at stake. The table is an attempt to demonstrate -- may I explain this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What has been deducted here, it's stated quite explicitly. I'm demonstrating how unreliable the sources are because when Mrs. Tabeau says that her sources are reliable and says that she matched the data up, and that's why I say Bakija is reliable and the census is reliable. I just used numbers to show that this is not correct. These are her figures. I didn't invent a single figure here. Whatever you match up, it's not logical because when you take what you have in one of the sources and what you have in one of the other sources, then the number of deaths due to natural causes seems to be greater than what you demonstrated to be the case. So what are you matching up? That was my question. And the table shows that there were illogical matters here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Just return to my question. You said Ms. Tabeau does the same. Could you please indicate where she does the same as you did on page 24, where you deducted from the number of buried Muslims from the Bakija data the killed Muslims from the 1994 survey.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Tabeau didn't calculate this in the same sense. She doesn't give a single table -- provide a single table from the Bakija source, but she provides figures in the text, and this is also manipulation to an extent. If you have a good source, you should demonstrate what you have managed to obtain on the basis of that source. Have a look at page 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Tabeau uses the data -- uses the Bakija source there. If you have a look at the last paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm looking at it. Page 18, last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Paragraph 4, 4.1, the source -- the database of the funeral parlour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The number in this database is 12.867, out of which 3.517 are marked with letter "B" for borac, that is to say, soldier. And 9.350 recorded by the letter "C" for civilian. These records covered the period from January 1992 to August 1996. The number of records for 1996 is less than in the respective period in 1992-1995. In general terms, we have 11.546 records from the period from January 1992 to December 1995. 3.414 soldiers, and 8.132 civilians, and 1.319 records covering the period from January 1996 to August 1996, (102 soldiers and 1.217 civilians) two records are illegible. Obviously the year of death was erroneous. Regarding the period from September 1992 to August 1994, the respective numbers are the following: Total, 6.266 soldiers, 2.000 -- the number of soldier, 2.024, and the number of civilians 4.242, so this is the number that Mrs. Tabeau obtained after matching up. This figure, if you use the figure from this source, from this table, it's the total number of records for those buried, and these figures are provided by Bakija since Bakija only buried Muslims and you can see this at the beginning of the text. And the second report that is a good one, a reliable one according to Mrs. Tabeau, and in demographic terms, in professional terms this is quite correct, it's quite legitimate, I adopted the number of -- the number of Muslims killed in order to arrive at this number. And in terms of statistical methods, this is also a correct procedure. I did this in order to see how many Bakija -- how many Muslims Bakija buried, who had died due to natural causes, and then there is something that is illogical because it seems that the number taken over by Mrs. Tabeau - and she says that Bakija worked inside the front lines and they buried Muslim there and so on - it turns out that Bakija buried a greater number of Muslims than the total number that refers to all other people, and this in my opinion is quite illogical.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, the question was, of which you still did not give an answer, why you disregarded that the Bakija is a more limited source, not covering the whole population but only that part of the population that would bury their dead through the Bakija parlour, why you deduct from then the overall -- the report on the population in general, so without limitations. That's the question. And you told us that Ms. Tabeau does the same. And my question was: Where does she do that? She does not do it in the part you just read to us. In one part she limits herself to the Bakija data and does not compare them in whatever way with the survey of 1994.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Statistically, demographically, scientifically, and professionally, this is not justified. She is duty-bound to compare them. If you are using different sources of information, regardless of whether they agree or not, and if you say that you are using different sources of information, well, if you do that, then you are duty-bound to make a comparative survey of that, of those data. And Mrs. Tabeau does not give us a comparative table from the sources which she says she's used for this purpose except in the text, and I'm trying to explain why she does not do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I again ask you: The question was not again what Ms. Tabeau did wrong but you are asked what you did on page 24. And Mr. Stamp alleges that you deducted from a number of a limited population, that is, the Bakija population, which does not claim to be -- Bakija was not claiming to serve the overall population -- why you deduct from those figures figures that relate to the overall population. That's, I think, the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not deducting it from the overall population but only the Muslim population. The source is Muslim because Bakija buries only Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The overall Muslim population deducted from limited, that is, Bakija, Muslim population. It doesn't change the question in a fundamental way.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't do anything else because I have the same sources as Mrs. Tabeau, that is, I am using Mrs. Tabeau's sources to show that they are wrong. Had I done the expertise for the Prosecutor's Office, I would have never done it in the manner in which Mrs. Tabeau did. My source is the expert opinion of Mrs. Ewa Tabeau. And I am not doing anything that I shouldn't do. I'm doing what one -- how would you please should do it. If you say that you had three, five, seven, half a source, but you have to show what those sources gave you; otherwise, you get a completely wrong picture, that is, that you have a wealth of data but what you conclude in the analysis needs to be supported by good statistical documentation, and I put it to you that that was not the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, I suggest to you that the statistical demographical scientific and professional method of estimating natural deaths and killed persons in the Bakija database would be applying the proportion, the proportion of natural deaths and killed persons obtained in the 1994 survey to the total from Bakija. Statistically speaking and in -- and professionally speaking you can only apply the proportion to come to a reasonable estimate. And if one did so, this would not change the general pattern of mortality presented in the report by Tabeau et al.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're wrong, sir. Mrs. Tabeau does it in table 17, and that is manipulation. She gives -- I don't know what the word used in Serbian "omeri," does, but I suppose it means ratios, of the event rates, et cetera, and again she gives only relative figures and does not mention any absolute figures. And it's just --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, that is a completely different thing to what I suggested to you. I'm just simply suggesting that to move across non-completely overlapping samples or sources you ought as a scientific, as a statistician, as a demographer, as a professional, to apply the proportion, take the proportion of killed to the proportion of natural deaths from one source to apply to the other to get an estimate, and that is the proper way. That is only what I had asked. Could we move on quickly.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're wrong.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a demographer -- you're suggesting to me the opposite. And what you're suggesting to me is not correct. As a demographer, I knew what I needed to do and that is what I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One or two things very quickly, since time is of the essence. You were shown 1928 by the Defence counsel. Could you have a look at it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, there is a new set of documents which is now numbered which will bear the number, Madam Registrar ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 1928A. It is the same document; however, the pages within the document have been numbered from number 1 through to number 132.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could I have a look at it, please. Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you were first shown that document, the Defence counsel showed you the document, showed you also two pages which indicated should have preceded the first page, the top page of that document, which the numbers end with "77." And Defence counsel indicated that they would get copies of that document, but I understand that they are not here. I'd like to add the first two pages. And perhaps it could be 1928C, to the -- and if I might remind you. Yesterday this is what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Radovanovic, I would like to remind you not to write on any of the documents unless specifically asked to do so. Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I apologise. I think we are short some copies. Having regard to the time, may we be allowed to proceed and we will provide copies later? I think the Defence had shown her those front pages on the first day the document was presented to her and had indicated that they would provide copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is my recollection as well. Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. As far as I remember, my colleague showed these two pages of the document. Pages 75, 76, which have to do with 98, and I think we have 77. I'll try to find them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, yesterday you made some comparisons and you indicated when asked by the President that you were using that document, that is, the document starting 00986275, containing figures in respect to sniping casualties, conclude that the figures presented by ET et al. were three times higher than the figure in this document. The first thing I'd like you to do is to put on the ELMO the document ending "275."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just indicate to the Court at the top of the document written in hand is EXD157. That should not be a part of it. As a matter of fact, this same document was tendered earlier in the case as D157.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's a recall of this document, in fact, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I don't think the entire 1978 -- there's a confusion in the document that I'm not even sure I understand, but I think D157 would be a part of some parts of 1928 and some parts of 1927. However, the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just look at that front part, madam, the section ending 6275. It's on the ELMO to your right. What does it say?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Survey of civilians killed and wounded by snipers between the 10th of September, 1992 to the 10th of August, 1994, identified so far in the city of Sarajevo."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, the document is on the ELMO to your right. Does it not say "survey of so far identified civilians killed and wounded"?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am reading it. "The survey of so far identified civilians killed and wounded due to sniping between the 10th of September, 1992 to the 10th of August, 1994 in the city of Sarajevo."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the part so far should indicate to any professional who is alert that the document is probably incomplete, wouldn't it? Wouldn't it, madam?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Know whether it is complete or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, you used this document, the completeness of which you know not about, to make comparisons to the survey of ET et al., and you said that this document had figures for sniping victims killed and wounded three times lower than those of ET et al. Look at the second page, please, at 276 -- ending 276, I beg your pardon. What's the total number of sniping victims killed?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said "no," I meant it didn't follow. I didn't mean no, it was not complete. You were asked me -- I'm sorry. I'm just trying to explain. Otherwise, you're right, I quoted three times more because it has to do with the sum total. It should be by 30 per cent less for the wounded and for the killed and almost twice as much for the wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us take it slowly. When you were first presented with this document on the first day when you testified and you were also presented with it the next day you testified, you said that having surveyed this document you found that in respect to the figures given by Tabeau et al. for killed civilians from sniping this document had three times less figures. You did it on two occasions, the first day testified, yesterday. You are now agreeing that you were wrong when you said that on two occasions?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are three times less in relation to the overall population. But since here we have only the civilians, my view was --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- That -- but I am trying to explain. Please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I just want us to understand certain things about these figures. Did Ms. Tabeau et al. give figures of sniping victims for 253 and isn't the figure for -- I beg your pardon the figure given by Tabeau et al. for sniping civilian victims is 253 and the figure given in this document, which you told the Court was three times lower, is in fact higher than the one given by Tabeau et al. Would you now agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I was dealing with the overall population --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, madam, you did not carefully peruse this document up until the time when you testified yesterday and the day before.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I went through the document very carefully, and I took out from it all the places about what you wanted to know anyone had been wounded there. My mistake was to take the wrong figure, and it can happen to anyone. But I was very careful and I knew what it was about. Rather than take figure 253, I took the figure of 566. I apologise. But it's not the three times higher number for the killed but it is by 30 per cent lower but is almost twice as -- the figure is almost twice as high for the wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, the two batches of documents that you were given -- that you were shown in the last couple days by the Defence, do you know what was the methodology used in collecting whatever information they might contain?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received the document from the Defence as a finished document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I've had the opportunity as a finished document. Will you define to me the way in which they came by this document. What do you want me to tell you? How they collected data?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Do you know how the information contained in any of those documents was collected, whether persons went to organisations to get them, whether they asked them to phone in, post in, how was it collected? By what method did they collect the information?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it has nothing to do with me. Sorry. I got the finished material.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Radovanovic, the question is whether you know how the data were collected. Either you know it; then please tell us. Or you don't know it; then please tell us that you don't know. It's as simple as that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I received the finished material. I do not know how the information was collected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The answer is you don't know. Mr. Stamp, would this be --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that you're asking for the time left for -- I'll just ask the -- you used your time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just ask a couple more questions with a document? It would not be more than five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll consider that during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll adjourn until twenty minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume a bit later than expected. That's because the Chamber would have to consider a few matters. First of all, the information that Mr. Piletta-Zanin is not available for health reasons. As a general rule, lead counsel takes over when co-counsel is not available. That's the general rule. The Chamber is willing, however, in order to accommodate you, Ms. Pilipovic, and also to give you an opportunity to consult with General Galic, to postpone the hearing on the submission on rebuttal evidence until next Friday but will not postpone the date on which we'll start with the -- Could we please wait for -- I apologise. But at the same time, invites the Prosecution to prepare to start perhaps with those witnesses that are available anyhow in The Hague, but if there are other practical issues, they could be discussed perhaps tomorrow. But the Prosecution should continue for its preparation to start with the rebuttal evidence in the beginning of next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That also means that if already the Defence could say in respect of certain witnesses that they would not object, if they can say that, they are invited to do that even before Friday. There might be evidence which is not objected by the Defence. I see you're nodding no, Ms. Pilipovic. But if that would be the case, then please inform the Prosecution as soon as possible. The Prosecution should inform the Defence even before Friday in which order they preferably would call the witnesses so that we could start at the beginning of next week. So the Chamber is willing to give you an extra opportunity to consult with General Galic, Ms. Pilipovic, but as a general rule, I repeat, that is that if co-counsel is not available, lead counsel is responsible for the continuation of the proceedings. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the three witnesses who are locally available are Roelof From, Linda Patrick and Jonathan Tait-Harris. Roelof From is available to give evidence on Monday, and indeed we plan to call him first. I can't imagine that the Trial Chamber or the Defence would wish to hear from Linda Patrick, whose 92 bis statement merely goes to identification and provision of some photographs shown to another witness who was the subject of a 92 bis statement. And it may well be that Jonathan Tait-Harris is also not required. Mr. President, the remaining witnesses all have to be brought from Sarajevo. And if we don't have a decision until Friday, it effectively means that we have to arrange for them all to come up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Before we know whether they're required or not. Mr. President, whilst I'm on my feet, just very briefly. I've given a courtesy copy of the filing to you through Madam Registrar. I notice that I've included two pages 4. The first of those should be withdrawn. There's an additional sentence added to paragraph 5 of the -- which appears on page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the explanation on your rebuttal evidence, is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. And in relation to the other document I've made available, I've also provided a copy of that to the Defence and a B/C/S copy. That is not intended as a filing but merely an aid to oral submissions to be made in relation to the admissibility of Mr. Radinovic's report, whenever that may be. So we certainly don't seek any written response from the Defence or -- or formal consideration by the Trial Chamber at this stage. It's simply to avoid 15 minutes of rattling off numbers. So Mr. President, coming back to the issue of the order of witnesses for next week. A decision on Friday does that have unfortunate and inevitable consequence that it may involve considerable expense and inconvenience to a number of people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That -- I do understand that it is expensive. At the same time, losing time in court is expensive as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean, the -- all the interpreters are ready to assist us, the technicians are there, the courtroom is there, so it's not a question of whether it's expensive or not but what would strike the best balance as far as the costs are concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, could I make some --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And apart from that, a case, of course, is not just a balance of costs, although we always keep them in the back of our mind, but it's also a matter of -- of proceeding towards what -- towards the end of the case. That's also a legal issue rather than just an economic issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I wonder whether perhaps we could finesse it to some extent. For instance, Witness G, I wonder whether his attendance would be required. The position in relation to him is there are some photographs taken of his back which are attached to the statement -- the 92 bis statement of the investigator Jonathan Tait-Harris. I wonder whether we really should be making arrangements for him to attend simply to show his back and -- although, I suppose there may be an issue of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Up till this moment we have not had a full opportunity to consider these matters. It's certainly not the case that the Chamber stops thinking until Friday. We'll continue to consider the matter. We'll -- but on the other hand, for final decisions we should hear the Defence as well. Therefore, the Defence is invited to say when there are no objections. But of course it's not -- we do not start -- we do not stop reading, we do not stop thinking, and therefore it's -- I could not exclude that some guidance would be given during the wait that if the Chamber would give certain decisions, that at least the Prosecution would not prepare in such a way that it would be counter-productive. Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour -- Your Honour, I merely wish to say that the Defence is preparing its response to the Prosecution's motion for rebuttal. However, today I've received a new seven-page-long document in English and new material for Mr. Veljko Zecevic [as interpreted] and some new material, that is, maps. Having in mind that my co-counsel is helping me with the preparations and work, since all this is in English, physically I'm not able to prepare our complete position in such a short time. I can work without my associate when I have time for full preparation. However, since I've received a new document today which I cannot study and analyse, it can only be a problem if I ask that the discussion about the rebuttal be done on Friday. So it is a short period of time that I need to prepare in the absence of my colleague. The material that I was given for Mr. Zecevic is again in English. It is two pages. So the problem for me is the physical preparation for our new position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just ask you: The Chamber received a courtesy copy of Mr. Zecevic's statements first in B/C/S and only afterwards, I think yesterday late, the English translation. But the B/C/S version was available on from the beginning, if I am correct. And I understood that --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's all right. But I'm just talking about the new document that I received today, the one referring to Mr. Berko Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it not a translation of the earlier document?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: From what I see displayed there, that appears to me to be the English translation of a part of the B/C/S document which was already given to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, this text is in English. This document is in English, the one that I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that would be a translation of part of the document that has been disclosed to you by way of courtesy last Friday, then this was rather for Mr. Piletta-Zanin than for you. But we could compare that. Perhaps during the next break this issue could be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, I think it's the English translation of annex D of the report, which was handed over on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. We could clarify that during the break. The Chamber has --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can check that today. If I can be provided with some information from the registry, I'd be grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we'll see how to solve that problem, but we don't have to spend time on it at this very moment. The Chamber decided that we would hear the parties Friday at quarter past 2.00 and to -- well, to be as flexible as possible in preparation for the situation that will exist. The Chamber also intends to give a decision, if it be only orally, next Friday as well, so that there's no further delay. At the same time, we all hope that Mr. Piletta-Zanin will recover soon, Ms. Pilipovic, and I take it that you'll pass these good wishes for recovery to Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. Your Honour, I am working on my preparations and I will provide a written submission. The Defence's position with regard to the rebuttal will be provided in a submission, and I think that I will file it by tomorrow. But the documents that I have received now and the new submission, which is seven pages long and is in English, perhaps this will prevent me from doing this immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I wonder whether it would be of any use and very exceptional to ask for some assistance, Ms. Pilipovic, that apart from having a final translation of this document, that it could be translated orally to you so that you at least have a -- an idea about the contents of it, because I -- the Chamber does understand that you are handicapped by the fact that you have no direct access to new English documents. So perhaps you could arrange for that, that someone sits next to you and reads the content of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'll familiarise myself with the contents of this document, but I don't know to what extent it will be possible for me to talk to General Galic about this document. I think it's a new submission, and this submission my colleague clarifies certain facts included -- contained in the previous submission, but I can't discuss this matter off the top of my head. Perhaps that is not the case. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if it's any assistance to Madam Pilipovic, I'm happy to arrange for a language assistant at a time to suit Ms. Pilipovic to sit with her and read through the document, to translate it orally while she takes note, if that would assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, whether you use this offer or not, Ms. Pilipovic, it's there. And I do understand that --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. My assistant is here. But it's not necessary. My young assistant is here, and he will inform me of the contents of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. The only thing I wanted to prevent is that next Friday we'd sit here and that we would be in the position that you have had no sufficient access to these documents in order to respond to the suggestions of the Prosecution. I now do see - Madam Registrar was helping us - that the English text you just received seems to be a translation of annex D of the statement of Professor Zecevic, and that was in the original filing in English was page 9190, ERN number of the original B/C/S version was 03266905.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar will assist you if you want to find out what document is exactly a translation of what.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I think we could resume the examination of the -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just before you do that, there is one other remaining matter, the exhibits of the witness Richard Gray.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We could do that, if that's convenient, after this witness finishes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What the Chamber -- what the Chamber intends to do is to deal as much as possible with whatever outstanding exhibits after we finish with this witness. And there is a long list of other exhibits as well, matters that we might have forgotten in the past. But the fifth tape and the video sequences is also one of the issues that we'll deal with after we finish this witness. Mr. Stamp, you have an additional five minutes for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please escort Ms. Radovanovic into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Radovanovic, you may expect a few more questions from the Prosecution and then the Defence will have an opportunity to ask additional questions. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, you may recall that one of the documents that I showed you and I read from, the publishers indicated that one of the major organisations that has published guidelines in respect to conducting initial demographic assessment in complex humanitarian emergencies was Medecins sans Frontieres, otherwise HSF -- I beg your pardon, MSF. Are you aware that they did a survey in Sarajevo during the period of the conflict in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you have a look at this document. There's a translation to the back. It indicates that "After exactly one year of war --" and if one could turn to the front. This is up to April 1993. "Population movements and the siege of Sarajevo MSF Holland has tried to get an overview of the situation in Sarajevo." And they indicate thereafter that they conducted a survey which covers fields including demography, including mortality. I'd like you to have a look at page 2, where it spoke of methodology. It is indicated: "On a few 'quiet' 3-5 April 1993, teams of MSF-Holland conducted a household survey in the more or less safe areas of Sarajevo, where about 65 per cent of the population is living. Thirty clusters of seven households were selected at random" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would you slow down, Mr. Stamp, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I apologise. I will endeavour to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "On a few quiet days, 3-5 April 1993, teams of MSF Holland conducted a household survey in the more or less safe areas of Sarajevo, where about 65 per cent of the population is living. Thirty clusters of seven households were selected at random, resulting in 210 households surveyed." And in the next paragraph, "A compromise was sought between the rapidity of the interview and the degree of detail of the answers." And it say that is the questionnaire is presented at annex 7. Firstly, this organisation could, for the purpose of an analysis for a complex humanitarian situation, use a definition of territory which is not standard to an analysis based on census methodology. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not this rapidly. I'd need the time to go through this carefully because I have the methodology here and they are mentioning the sample they used. They're not mentioning the procedure followed. That is the difference. If you grant me a little time to read through this, I'll do so. But naturally, I don't contest the fact that it's possible to use a sample to do all sorts of things in statistics. I'm bringing into question Mrs. Tabeau's sample because it was taken from totally unreliable and biased sources. But I don't say that it's impossible to do this. What's at stake is a sample.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was really asking about definition of territory in a complex humanitarian situation. You see, they have used safe areas as their definition of territory.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find that. If you could indicate where I could find this. It says, "In more or less safe parts," and they took a random sample. They didn't say they were going from house to house, as in the case of the census used by Mrs. Tabeau. They didn't compile a list of all the households that had such cases. They were in "more or less safe areas" and they had a sample of 30 groups in which there were seven households. They couldn't have made any mistakes there. 30 people were given the task of visiting seven households. They would return with this material in the evening. They'd need a few days for this. And then they'd say, "Look, we have obtained -- we've found 909 people in these households." And this is not something I would contest, these samples that are used in statistics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at page 11 in section 4.2.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have page 11. Sorry, where is it? In my report?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There should be a translation of page 11 at the back of your document. Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's a translation headed --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or I can't find it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... "4.2 Mortality." There you go. That is the page beginning, "/Prevod sa engleskog jezika" 4.2, mortality. And there they give a mortality rate for the year period that they studied of 0.63 per 10.000 per day, confidence interval 0.32 to 0.96. And in the next paragraph, it is indicated that the mortality rate is extrapolated to the population of Sarajevo which was assessed at 350.000, and it would mean 8.050 deaths per year, of which 4.600 deaths would be because of violence. Madam, it is clear that -- well, would you agree with me, firstly, that the organisation MSF is a reputable international organisation in the field of international humanitarian matters including statistics and demography?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't agree with that because I know very little about that organisation with respect to carrying out statistic and demographic research. I haven't had the opportunity of viewing any study made by theirs, any study that wasn't for internal purposes. So I'm not able to have an opinion on this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I suggest to you that the reason why you're unaware of it and can't put forward an opinion is because the area of demography and statistics and epidemiology in international humanitarian crises is alien to you because your expertise is in census, the census domain of demography.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I say that you are not right. I work for a university that has a demography department. I'm the head of the department for demography and I lecture in three subjects. The first one is called the statistics of the population, and that includes census statistics and vital statistics. The second subject is called demography. And the third subject is called ethnodemography. If this doesn't mean that I am sufficiently qualified, then I can say that I have published over 50 scientific articles that deal with demography, mortality, birthrates, and the smallest number has to do with population censuses because for me the results of censuses served as a basis for applying statistics and demographic methods in demography. In addition to that, often participate in projects of the European University for Peace. I am interested in demographic matters, mortality, birthrates, and the dynamics of population movement. And apart from that, I am also participating in two projects at my university at the moment. One is called "Population Migrations," and I am the head of a subproject --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am just trying to tell you what my qualifications are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... In your answer you have not really addressed the distinctions I was making. I was referring to a particular area of demography that I am suggesting you are clearly not familiar with it. I am not saying that your experience in demography generally is incomplete, but whether you have expertise in the particular area of demography that we are concerned with here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Lastly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this will really be your last question, Mr. Stamp. Five minutes are --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed. Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll put it this way: Assuming that if one converts the mortality rate given by Medecins sans Frontieres for the first year of the war to a rate per 100.000 per annum and the result would be approximately -- not approximated, it would be exactly 2.099,5 for 100.000 per annum or 4.599 for 1.000 per two years, it would indicate that their rate is higher, about twice as high, as a rate given by Tabeau et al. at page 40 of the report. Assuming -- assuming that my mathematics is correct when you convert it, would that not indicate that apart from the fact that the rates were higher in the first few months and the first year of the conflict, it also indicates that Tabeau et al. were correct when they say that they -- that their study was done to find the absolute minimum possible casualties? It's a long question, so perhaps you could read it.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't read it because I don't know English, but I think I've understood the essence. You are asking me to compare pears and apples. You have provided me with a document which refers to the year 1993, and it was a sort of pilot research carried out on a sample which wasn't taken on every single day in the course of 1993 but it was a sample that consists of 30 clusters of seven households. And Mrs. Tabeau -- I really have nothing against them, I'm not saying that MSF and demographers don't know how to do the calculations, but this is a different matter. I don't say that rates per 100.000 are used, but this is a different matter, and it's far more correct procedure. They've provided the daily rate and this is quite correct. And then they say the confidence interval. They have provided certain restrictions. They said what the confidence interval was. And Mrs. Tabeau did not do this. She has a period of time which is far more extensive, and I am not criticising Mrs. Tabeau for having used rates per 100.000. What I am saying is that the justification that it's a small number of people, this isn't correct, or rather, the rates are not based on reliable information, on reliable sources, because they are -- the sources are biased, they are not complete, et cetera. And this is data that Mrs. Tabeau uses and cites as the sources that she has used. This is what we are discussing. I have nothing against this report. I am not claiming that it's not a good report, and I'm not saying that you don't use rates per 100.000, but I'm just saying that the procedure -- I'm just contesting the procedure and the method of Mrs. Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President, Your Honours, for your patience. May it please you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Pilipovic, is there any need to re-examine the witness? The Chamber would very much like to finish with this witness today. We also would like at least to make a start with the --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one question. And yes, Your Honour. Your Honour, I have one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Re-examined by Ms. Pilipovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Professor Radovanovic, in the course of his cross-examination the Prosecutor suggested, I think, that the data on the basis of which Mrs. Tabeau compiled her report come from a questionnaire and not from the census and you denied this. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I claim that this information is from the census.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us why you made such a claim.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, apart from the word where it says that it seems like it -- it appears -- that it looks like a questionnaire, that the census looks like a questionnaire, the word "questionnaire" doesn't appear anywhere again but the word "census" is used in the tables. But I know it's a census. I got the original questionnaire where this research was carried out. Could you have a look at annex 1 in the Serbian version. Could you have a look at the questionnaire, at the poll. The questionnaire is as follows: It says "questionnaire" or "poll for recording the households in the free areas of the city of Sarajevo in 1994." It doesn't say -- it says "questionnaire."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have Mrs. Tabeau's report in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you have a look at page 56 in the Serbian version.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it say "questionnaire" there?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
